The Great Honolulu Chinatown Fire. To control a bubonic plague outbreak, health authorities set fire to several houses, but the fire burned for 17 days and spread over 38 acres. Honolulu. 1900

A wave of bubonic plague was introduced to Honolulu on October 20, 1899 through a shipment of rice which had been carrying rats. Plague infected 11 people. The response by the Board of Health included incinerating garbage, renovating the sewer system, putting Chinatown under quarantine, and most of all burning infected buildings. 41 fires were set, but on January 20, 1900 winds picked up and the fire spread to other buildings. The runaway fire burned for seventeen days and destroyed 4,000 houses over 38 acres (15 Ha) of Honolulu. The fire campaign continued for another 31 controlled burns after the initial fire was brought under control. The 7,000 homeless residents were housed in detention camps and the quarantine was maintained until April 30. A total of 40 people died of the plague.
